project.name: orgii
project.description: ORG-2 (orgii) is an open-source, Cursor-style agent IDE: a Tauri desktop app pairing a React/TypeScript frontend with a Rust (Axum/Tokio) backend, built as a session-oriented developer workstation for orchestrating, chatting with, and reviewing multiple coding agents alongside git, code-editing, browser, and terminal tooling.

nodes.name: Agent Chat & Live Sessions
nodes.summary: Handles real-time conversation with AI coding agents: composing and sending messages, streaming agent responses into the transcript, and rendering interactive tool prompts (question batches, mode switches) and inline canvases/artifacts as the agent works.

businessRules: A session must be bound to exactly one live adapter (CLI, rust-agent, Cursor IDE, or external history) at a time
Streaming deltas are buffered and coalesced before committing to the event store to avoid excessive re-renders
Interactive tool prompts (ask-question, mode-switch) block further input until resolved
crossDomainInteractions: Delegates work-item execution and plan approvals to Agent Orgs & Automation
Persists finished sessions for later playback in Session Replay & Simulation
Reads provider credentials from the Credential & Model Provider Vault to authenticate adapters

nodes.name: Send Message & Stream Agent Response
nodes.summary: User composes a message, it is dispatched through a session adapter to the underlying agent process, and the streamed response is buffered and rendered live as chat blocks.

nodes.name: Compose message in input area

nodes.name: Submit via floating composer
nodes.summary: The composed message is submitted through the floating composer / ComposerInput widget.

nodes.name: Dispatch to session adapter

nodes.name: Open transport & event handler
nodes.summary: The adapter opens a transport/process channel and wires up an event handler for incoming agent events.

nodes.name: Buffer streaming deltas

nodes.name: Render streamed content as blocks
nodes.summary: Chat blocks (messages, tool calls, canvases) are rendered from the routed activity stream.

nodes.summary: When the agent needs user input mid-run, the chat surface renders question batches or an execution-mode switch card, captures the user's choice, and feeds it back into the running session.

nodes.name: Handle exec-mode switch
nodes.summary: A mode-switch card lets the user change the agent's execution mode mid-conversation.

nodes.name: Render Inline Canvas / Artifacts
nodes.summary: Agent turns that produce UI artifacts (A2UI payloads or React components) are detected, built, policy-checked, and rendered inline in the chat transcript, with an option to open them full-size in the Simulator.

nodes.summary: A completed turn is checked for an associated canvas payload.

nodes.name: Agent Orgs & Automation Orchestration
nodes.summary: Defines multi-agent organizations and workflows, schedules and recovers work items assigned to agents, gates risky actions behind plan approvals, and executes lifecycle hooks and MCP tool bridges around agent runs.

businessRules: Work items must go through the scheduler before being dispatched to an agent
A proposed plan requiring approval blocks further execution until approved or rejected
Hooks are dispatched for defined lifecycle events and can veto or modify agent behavior
Watchdog monitors org runs and can recover or restart stuck work items
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes chat sessions from Agent Chat & Live Sessions as the execution surface for agents
Reads/writes work items shared with Project & Work Item Management
Relays external notifications through Integrations & Cloud Collaboration channel gateway
Resolves model credentials via the Credential & Model Provider Vault

nodes.name: Session Replay & Simulation
nodes.summary: Lets users play back a previously recorded agent session step by step, reconstructing code diffs and browser activity per turn, and hosts simulator apps (canvas, background tasks) that render agent-produced artifacts outside the live chat.

businessRules: Replay is read-only and reconstructs state purely from recorded events, never re-executes the agent
Each simulator app declares a config used to match which events it can render
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes recorded sessions produced by Agent Chat & Live Sessions
Uses cross-tool projections from Cross-Tool Activity Tracking to reconstruct blame/diff timelines
Renders diffs alongside data from Git Workflow & Version Control

nodes.name: Cross-Tool Activity Tracking (Orgtrack)
nodes.summary: Ingests session history produced by other coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor CLI/IDE, Codex, Cline) from disk, normalizes it, and projects it onto files and repos as blame, stats, and replay data so all agent activity is trackable in one place.

businessRules: Ingested history must be normalized into a shared session model regardless of source tool
Privacy redaction is applied before external history is surfaced in the UI
crossDomainInteractions: Feeds file-level blame/timeline data into Git Workflow & Version Control
Supplies replay projections consumed by Session Replay & Simulation
Surfaces GitHub/work-item activity in Project & Work Item Management

nodes.name: Detect installed tool history/DB files

nodes.summary: Parse Claude Code's session history format.

nodes.name: Parse Cursor/Codex/Cline history

nodes.name: Normalize into shared session model

nodes.name: Project & Work Item Management
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle of trackable work items — creation, agent assignment, scheduling, and review — and presents them through Kanban, Gantt, and calendar views, plus syncs with external trackers like Linear and GitHub Issues.

businessRules: A work item can be scheduled to run on a cron-like recurrence
Work item state transitions are driven by replayed agent-run events, not just manual edits
External work items (Linear, GitHub) are cached locally and paginated for the UI
crossDomainInteractions: Assigns work items to agents managed by Agent Orgs & Automation Orchestration
Displays orgtrack-projected agent activity from Cross-Tool Activity Tracking
Pulls GitHub issues via Integrations & Cloud Collaboration's GitHub integration

nodes.name: Git Workflow & Version Control
nodes.summary: Wraps local git operations end to end: watching repo status, staging/committing/branching/merging/stashing, generating AI-assisted commit messages, reviewing diffs and blame, and managing worktrees and remotes.

businessRules: Repo status watching must debounce filesystem events to avoid UI thrash
AI commit suggestions are generated from staged diff content only
Worktree operations must not clobber an existing checked-out branch
crossDomainInteractions: Diff and blame data is enriched with orgtrack session blame from Cross-Tool Activity Tracking
File tree and diff state feed the Code Editing & Language Tooling editor surface
GitHub-specific operations delegate to Integrations & Cloud Collaboration's GitHub client

Workspace root detection determines which project config drives LSP behavior
crossDomainInteractions: Shares file/diff state with Git Workflow & Version Control
Hosts the diff/replay viewer used by Session Replay & Simulation
Editor actions are invoked as tool calls from Agent Chat & Live Sessions

edges.description: Live chat sessions execute within org-defined workflows; plan approvals and hooks gate agent actions taken in chat.
Finished live sessions become recordings that can be replayed turn by turn.
Agent tool calls in chat drive the embedded browser and terminal engines.
Session adapters resolve model credentials from the vault before connecting.
Agent tool calls open, edit, and diff files in the code editor.
Replay reconstructs diffs and blame using orgtrack's session projections.
Orgtrack projects per-file session blame alongside native git blame and history.
Orgtrack-derived session artifacts and stats are surfaced in WorkManagement views.
Scheduled work items are dispatched to org-defined agents for execution.
Org/agent model selection resolves provider credentials from the vault.
The notification channel gateway relays external chat messages into org agent inboxes.
The editor's file tree and diff panes react to live git status and diff data.
GitHub issues are imported as work items via the GitHub integration.
PR base-ref resolution and remote sync interoperate with the GitHub integration client.
Captured browser sessions are replayed alongside code diffs in Session Replay.
